what: WHO HELD WHAT, AND WHEN -- one row per tenure, lifted out of the prose chains in arda_artifacts.json and given a holder that resolves to a record. §VI `relationships/ownership/`.
not_a_new_population: EVERY ROW IS ONE `ch` ENTRY OF ONE ARTIFACT, carrying that entry's own `when` and its own `cite` unchanged. Nothing is added to the history and nothing is dated here. What is new is the HOLDER, as an id.

how_a_holder_is_resolved.the index: map/ardaentity.py, built from the collections that DEFINE ids -- the genealogy, the Ainur, the creatures, the epithets, the gazetteer, the realms -- read off `git -C site ls-files`, never a glob.
how_a_holder_is_resolved.the match: whole words, through ardatext.words_of, which is the archive's ONE matcher. Never a raw lower(): the datasets are mixed NFC/NFD exactly as the corpus is, and Fëanor typed one way does not equal Fëanor typed the other.
how_a_holder_is_resolved.one word of a person's name is a match,: prose does not use full names. `Thingol — set in the Nauglamír` names a person the archive holds as `Elu Thingol`; matching full names only called 19 of 62 tenures empty and every one of those absences was false. A single word of a PERSON's name is therefore in the matching vocabulary, and every edge records `matched_by` so a reader can tell it from a full-name match. PERSONS ONLY: splitting place names would put `Minas`, `Amon` and `Haudh` -- common nouns of Sindarin -- into the vocabulary.
how_a_holder_is_resolved.a place is not a holder: a place or realm standing in tenure prose goes to `place_or_realm_named`, never to `held_by`. Reading it as a bearer was this file's first fault: `Fëanor — at Formenos` produced Formenos as a holder and 50 of 113 edges were places.
how_a_holder_is_resolved.the longest name wins, and only by conta: `Beren Erchamion` and `Beren` are both in the index; where one matched name is contained in another, only the longer stands. Two unrelated names both present both stand -- a tenure can have two holders.
how_a_holder_is_resolved.ambiguity is published, never resolved: a name borne by more than one record yields a holder with `entity: null` and every candidate named. The owner's ruling of 5 August: publish the correspondence, do not choose a winner.

the_artifact_id_is_minted_here: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: arda_artifacts.json carries no `id` on any of its rows. `af_<slug>` is derived from the record's own name, it is unique to this file, and `source_record` carries the dataset, the collection and the index so it can be followed back. Where exactly one arda_artifact_prompts caption normalises to the same name that correspondence is published; where none or several do it is NOT RESOLVED, because a fuzzy match between `Narsil / Andúril` and `Narsil and Anduril` would be this file deciding which artifact a prompt is about.

silence_is_split_in_two_and_never_blurre.searched and empty: the tenure's prose was matched against every name the entity index holds and none of them stands in it. The row publishes the size of that index (C224). This is a statement about the ARCHIVE'S REGISTERS -- no search of the corpus was run for it, and none is implied.
silence_is_split_in_two_and_never_blurre.ambiguous: a name that matched more than one record. Not an absence at all: the archive holds several, and the row names them.

the_deed_and_the_year_are_two_confidence: Where the artifact record's citation qualifies the YEAR separately from the DEED -- the Nauglamir's citation marks the making [C] and then marks [I-M] on the absence of an annal for its year -- the row carries BOTH: `conf` for the deed and `date_conf` for the year. The owner's ruling of 11 August, and the pattern is the gazetteer's `name_conf`/`place_conf` on 481 places. Reading the weakest marker anywhere in the citation, as this file did at first, marked a canon making as inferred because the ANNAL for its year is missing. WHERE EVERY MARKER QUALIFIES THE DATE the deed carries none of its own, and `conf` is HELD at the weaker value rather than promoted: the deed is cited by book and the citation does not mark it, and inferring [C] from an absent marker would be filling a silence with something reasonable.
the_artifact_form_is_not_an_entity_kind: `artifacts[].form` holds what the thing IS -- jewel, ring, sword, helm, phial. It was called `kind` until map/classvocab_check.py pooled it with the `kind` on every resolved holder and scored eight artifact forms as rare values in a vocabulary of 76 `person`. Two classifications under one key name is this archive's oldest fault shape; measured apart, the forms are 11 distinct over 20 uses (free text) and the holder kinds are 3 over 127 (closed).
manner_is_not_a_judgement_of_right: `manner` records the words the tenure's own prose uses -- taken, given, made, borne, found, lost. Morgoth held the Silmarils and the register says so; `taken` is what keeps that row from reading as ownership by right. The patterns are published below.
artifacts_what: One row per artifact, with the id this file mints and what it corresponds to elsewhere. NOT a new artifact register: arda_artifacts.json is still the record, and this holds only what an ownership edge needs to point at.
